arguments.value: HPIL EnergyTech and GINARES agreed to work together for one year to cooperate on expanding GINARES’s renewable energy projects, especially its waste-to-fuel technology. Each side will keep the other informed, collaborate as needed, and develop target projects and goals within six months. The agreement is non-exclusive, creates no employment or partnership relationship, and does not provide for payment or compensation. Both parties must keep shared information confidential, comply with applicable anti-corruption and export-control laws, and bear their own expenses. Each party makes standard legal promises about authority, compliance, and no pending litigation, and agrees to indemnify the other for losses caused by breaches or inaccurate statements. Disputes must be resolved by ICC arbitration in Paris under Nevada law, though urgent court relief is allowed if needed.
